objective: Make Hermes job discovery behave like the owner's successful Codex workflow: actively research the open web for current entry-level cybersecurity opportunities, not merely scan a fixed provider list. Add a bounded, read-only web-research lane that searches broad web results (including public LinkedIn Jobs/Indeed/Google-indexed job results and employer ATS/career pages when discoverable), validates source URLs, normalizes findings into the existing unified discovery schema, and sends them through the already-built semantic triage -> deterministic eligibility -> dedupe -> tracker/Chief handoff funnel.
prerequisites: Reuse the completed high-recall/unified-discovery implementation already on main.
Do not modify or weaken the existing deterministic eligibility, dedupe, owner-approval or no-external-mutation gates.
Respect the 2026-09-23 safety directive: no local interactive browser/GUI automation, no signed-in browser profiles/cookies/sessions.
allowed_scope: First inspect the earlier Codex-driven job-search workflow/config/prompts still present on disk/repo and determine how it obtained web results; preserve useful query patterns rather than guessing.
Implement a Web Research discovery collector as another SOURCE_REGISTRY surface feeding the exact same unified candidate schema; do not create a parallel tracker, classifier or eligibility engine.

Primary behavior must be active research, not a static provider scan: generate/search a query matrix across role families (graduate/new-grad/junior/associate/analyst/L1/SOC/GRC/IAM/technology risk/security operations/information security/cybersecurity) and configured regions.

Use Codex as the research worker when its available runtime can perform current web research; test this capability explicitly. If Codex CLI cannot browse/search in the installed runtime, fail truthfully and implement a provider interface/fallback rather than pretending it searched.

Search the open web broadly enough to discover public job-result URLs from LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed and Google-indexed job pages/search results where accessible, plus direct employer careers/ATS domains such as Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Teamtailor, Workable, HRMOS/HERP/Jobcan and other source URLs found by the research worker.

Do not log into LinkedIn/Indeed/Google, do not use cookies/session state, do not scrape behind authentication, do not solve CAPTCHAs, and do not drive a local browser. Public/search-index discovery only.

For each discovered vacancy preserve provenance: search query, discovery surface, result URL, canonical URL if resolved, employer/title/location as observed, fetched/validated state, source timestamp and any missing fields. Never invent a vacancy from a search snippet.

Where safe HTTP retrieval is available, validate that the destination exists and extract only source-supported fields; otherwise keep it as a discovered-but-unverified candidate and label that status explicitly.
Resolve cross-source duplicates so a vacancy seen on LinkedIn, Indeed, Google/search, an ATS and Company Watch becomes one canonical candidate with all provenance retained.

Use the existing DeepSeek bulk semantic triage and bounded Codex second pass after collection. Do not spend Codex review calls over the entire raw web-result universe; web research and semantic review are separate budgeted stages.

Add per-source/funnel telemetry: queries_executed, results_seen, candidate_urls, validated_live, validation_failed, duplicates_collapsed, semantically_reviewed, deterministic_eligibility_pass, tracker_candidates, and zero attribution. A zero result must distinguish search-source failure, no accessible results, validation failure, filtering, eligibility and dedupe.

Add company-watchlist hooks so an owner-provided list of companies can later be searched explicitly by company + cybersecurity role family in addition to the general market search. Do not require the list to exist to finish the generic search agent.
Keep schedules dry-run/read-only initially. Do not enable canonical workbook writes automatically. Produce a candidate manifest + Chief summary for review.
Add tests with captured public-search fixtures proving LinkedIn/Indeed/ATS result normalization, source provenance, cross-source collapse and fail-closed behavior for inaccessible/unverified results.

Run a bounded live research acceptance if the available Codex/web path supports it. Record exact queries, source classes, candidate counts and URLs privately/safely; no fabricated PASS if web access is unavailable.
Update Career Ops README, roster/state/tracker and acceptance docs. Commit and push in checkpointed units.
stop_conditions: No job applications, employer/recruiter outreach, LinkedIn posts/messages/connections or account mutations.
No interactive browser/GUI automation and no use of signed-in browser profiles/cookies/session secrets.
No claim that LinkedIn/Indeed/Google Jobs were searched unless the actual live research evidence proves those source classes were reached.
No fabricated jobs, titles, employers, URLs, JDs, eligibility or sponsorship facts.
Do not bypass robots/auth/CAPTCHA/access controls or implement stealth/evasion scraping.
If a source blocks public access, record it as unavailable and continue other sources.
notes: This is intentionally different from the existing provider scanner. The owner wants the successful Codex behavior: active, broad web research for jobs, while retaining the new Career Ops reliability, semantic filtering, provenance, dedupe and tracker controls.

result.summary: Attempt-3 resume of the open-web research lane (B26). Repository inspected first: attempts 1-2 had landed the implementation, tests, fixtures, acceptance runner and six evidence bundles but never committed them (both died on dispatch timeouts, not on a real blocker). Resume work: (1) re-verified the landed lane at HEAD (Codex CLI resolved from %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin, codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.3, real web_search events proven); (2) found and fixed a real truthfulness gap — a bounded live pass reached 13 real URLs of which 11 were the boards' own search/listing pages (LinkedIn /jobs/<keywords>, Indeed /q-..., Reed ...-jobs-in-<place>) and 7 of them passed the deterministic gates as tracker candidates; every URL is now classified from the URL alone (classify_result_kind -> job_posting/search_listing/unknown) and the source-agnostic gate refuses search_listing, so a search page can never be written as a job; (3) produced the reviewable candidate manifest + Chief summary (0 rows, truthful: every live-discovered URL was a listing page or failed liveness validation); (4) corrected a misquote in the lane's provenance text ('Each query triggers a WebSearch' was attributed to portals.yml; the real wording and the Level-3 WebSearch/liveness rules live in modes/scan.md — verified read-only against the owner's install); (5) committed and pushed in 7 checkpointed units. Delivered: career-ops/discovery/web_research.py (generated query matrix across role families x regions x surfaces with the owner's site: shapes preserved, research-worker interface codex-web-search/captured/none, per-result provenance, robots-respecting read-only HTTP validation, telemetry + zero attribution, optional company-watchlist hook), wired into discovery/pipeline.py as SOURCE_WEB_RESEARCH feeding the ONE existing funnel (semantic triage -> deterministic eligibility -> dedupe -> tracker/Chief). No application, outreach, login, cookie/session, CAPTCHA bypass or browser/GUI action occurred; raw result URLs stay in the git-ignored runtime directory and committed evidence is aggregate only. Every live claim is backed by committed evidence; earlier FAIL bundles were kept as history rather than overwritten.
